objective: Lower BUKLOD MAIN sponsored-video cached egress without compromising immediate visible autoplay, near-viewport preload, player caching, AdMob ad fill or legal paid impression accounting. Stage optional smaller-quality video renditions, retain existing player briefly on scroll-back, and define precise monthly quota threshold evaluations.
productionBaselineEvidence: 2026-11-19: Live Supabase BUKLOD MAIN yhanxndaqbmuzbdqlblu has one historical 48.54MB sponsored MP4 with 3,688 Nov 12 CDN cache hits; no currently approved active video campaigns. User screenshot shows 391.87 GB / 250 GB organization cached egress. Current CommunityVideo already caches 256MB, mounts only visible plus one next warm slot and uses poster/handoff. Sponsored-video component has Android useCaching:true and 120ms near-viewport geometry prewarm. No official organization-wide billing usage API exposed to connected Supabase connector.
chosenApproach: Preserve original video_url, native cache, visible autoplay and one-screen prebuffer. Add optional verified 720p and low 480p MP4 URLs selected once per campaign based on network hints; pause immediately on leaving visibility, retain near-viewport decoder only 1.25s for short scroll-back, release immediately on tab unfocus. Add fully local fast-start H264/AAC encoder with byte-saving checks for operator-delivered variants. Add authoritative-source-only 50/70/85/95 quota threshold evaluator with UNVERIFIED fallback. Provide a trusted, dry-run-first offline upload/promotion command using existing Supabase SDK; it verifies SHA, faststart and HTTP HEAD before optionally recording variants, never modifies original URL.
selectionRationale: Dominant cached-egress spike is large public sponsored MP4 repeatedly requested. Smaller rendition files save most bytes while preserving first frame; player hold avoids transient range-request churn. No blanket autoplay disable, deferred visible playback, or aggressive prefetch deletion. Cloud transcoding and billing ingestion require separately verified runtime source and are not falsely claimed.
alternativeApproaches: Global 30-second tap-to-play or disabling video ads: rejected because destroys first-view rendering and revenue.
Changing paid ad impression or rotation policies: rejected because monetary/revenue functions are protected.
Client-side ffmpeg runtime or paid media API: rejected because requires large native dependencies, build, device performance and potentially cost.
Assuming edge-log counts are official organization monthly egress: rejected because request counts are not billing bytes.
